summary: This diff closes 4 real, well-scoped HR gaps (expense reimbursement, employee loans/advances, KRA/360 appraisal, shift roster) with a clean additive Drizzle migration (org-scoped RLS+FORCE+policies+grants+indexes mirroring the existing 0050 convention), correctly wired payroll integration (loan installment deduction and expense reimbursement earning line inside processPayrollRun, guarded against double-processing since only draft runs are processable), sensible pure-function unit tests for the schedule/weighted-score/shift-resolution logic, and honest registry/exemption entries; no changes touch .github/workflows/** so the workflow-scope hard rule does not apply. Architecture and correctness are sound and match established codebase conventions (auth-guard usage, service-layer validation, tenant-scoped queries). Two authorization gaps are worth the human merger's attention before/at sign-off, detailed in issues, but neither is a data-corrupting or directly fund-moving defect given the manager-approval gate still sits in front of any real money movement, so this is ready for human sign-off per the tier2 process rather than a hard reject.
issues: src/app/api/hr/loans/route.ts POST + hr-loan-service.ts requestLoan(): unlike every other self-service action in this module (leave requests, expense claims all key off the caller's own ctx.userId), requestLoan() accepts an arbitrary `employeeId` in the request body with no check that it matches the caller and no requireRole gate on the route -- any authenticated non-manager employee can create a pending loan/advance request attributed to any other employee in the org. Blast radius is bounded (a manager must still approve before any installment schedule/deduction is generated), but it's a real inconsistency versus this same PR's own hr-expense-service.ts pattern and should either restrict employeeId to the caller's own employeeProfiles row or require a manager/HR role to create a loan on someone else's behalf.

GET /api/hr/expenses (and /api/hr/loans, /api/hr/shifts/roster) let any authenticated org member list every other employee's records -- for expenses this includes amount/description/receiptUrl -- when the `userId`/`employeeId` filter is omitted, since there's no requireRole gate on the list endpoints. This exactly mirrors this repo's pre-existing convention on /api/hr/leave-requests, so it is not a regression introduced by this PR, but expense/loan amounts are more sensitive than leave dates -- worth a follow-up decision on whether HR financial list endpoints should require a manager role by default.
